CZ/SK Payroll Declarations

The common ground of the Czech and Slovak payroll filings — the Payroll Declarations menu, the Generate / Mark Submitted workflow, corrections, form versions, and how payslips are read from either payroll engine.

What it is for

Every Czech and Slovak payroll filing in this localization — the monthly social and health insurance reports, the tax overviews, the pension record sheets, the registrations — is a separate module. They all work the same way, because they are built on this one. This page describes what they have in common; each form's own page describes its content.

The module adds the Payroll Declarations menu, the version table of the statutory forms, and the machinery behind every filing record: the period, the states, the XML export with its schema check, corrections, and the reading of payslips. It depends neither on Odoo Enterprise Payroll nor on the OCA payroll app; it reads payslips from whichever of the two is installed. It installs itself as a dependency of the forms and does nothing on its own.

The workflow

Every form appears under Payroll Declarations as its own menu item. A filing record covers one company and one period:

  1. New, then choose the Year and Month. Both default to the current month, so change them when preparing last month's filing. The record shows the period's first and last day. Payment Date is the payday reported where the form asks for one (on the Slovak forms denVyplaty); left empty, the period end is used.
  2. Check the Version (see Form versions). The picker offers only the versions of the form being prepared.
  3. Click Generate. The module checks the master data the form needs (each form adds its own checks — company identifiers, birth numbers, addresses), collects the period's payslips, builds one row per employee, renders the XML, checks it against the official XSD and attaches it. The state becomes Generated.
  4. Download the XML and file it on the authority's portal. No form in the family sends anything by itself.
  5. Click Mark Submitted. The XML that was generated becomes the Filed XML, is added to the Filed history, the date is recorded, and the record is locked: it can neither be regenerated nor deleted.
  6. Reset to Draft unlocks it again. The filed copy and the history are kept, so what was actually sent stays on record even if the figures are regenerated later.

Confirm the period's payslips before generating: drafts are not counted (see Which payslips are counted).

Generating stops with a message when the period has no payslips, when no version applies, or when the XML does not pass the schema. Every step is logged in the chatter.

Corrections

The authorities accept amendments to a filing they already have, and each spells them differently — opravný, dodatočný, storno. The record has a Correction Type with up to four values, shown in English:

Value Meaning
Regular the ordinary filing for the period
Corrective replaces a filing already sent
Supplementary adds to a filing already sent, which stays valid
Cancellation withdraws a filing that should not have been sent

A form offers only the values its authority accepts, and only those that have been checked against the authority's rules. At present:

Form Correction types offered
SK Prehľad o zrazených a odvedených preddavkoch Regular, Corrective
SK Hlásenie o vyúčtovaní dane Regular, Corrective, Supplementary
CZ PPPZ Regular, Corrective
all other forms Regular only — file corrections on the portal

For anything other than Regular, Generate refuses unless a filing of the same form for the same company and period is already Submitted — an amendment to something never filed would be rejected. The period is compared by its first and last day, so for an annual form the month the record was created in does not matter. Where the authority needs to match the amendment to the original, enter its reference in Correction Reference.

An amendment is built from the period's payslips as they are now, exactly like the regular filing; see Limitations.

Which payslips are counted

Unless a form's own page says otherwise, a filing for a period counts every payslip of the company that

  • ends inside the period — a payslip belongs to the period its end date falls in, so one crossing a month or year boundary is counted exactly once, in the period where it ends, and
  • is confirmed: Done on the OCA engine, Validated or Paid on Enterprise. Draft payslips (and Waiting ones on the OCA engine) are ignored, as are cancelled ones. Confirm the period's payslips before clicking Generate.

From those payslips the module sums the salary-rule lines by code, per employee and in total. The rule codes differ slightly between the Enterprise and OCA engines (for example the Slovak income tax advance is one line on the OCA engine and one line per tax band on Enterprise); the module knows both spellings, so a form gives the same result on either engine.

Each employee row also carries, by default:

Row value Taken from
assessment base (Vz Base) the employee's GROSS for the period
insured days (Insured Days) the days of employment inside the period, read from all the employee's contract versions (contract start and end); the whole period when no version has a contract start date
worked hours (Worked Hours) the hours of all the employee's worked-days lines, absences included

Individual forms take these values or compute their own; check the form's page.

Form versions

The authorities change their forms and schemas from time to time. Each form vintage is a record under Payroll Declarations → Configuration → Declaration Versions: report code, country, Valid From / Valid To, the XML template, the expected root element and the XSD file. A new vintage is shipped as a new version record with its own template and schema; old vintages stay available.

A new filing record proposes the version of its form that is valid today in the country of your current company, and changes it when you change the year or month. Generate settles it: it switches to the version of this form valid for the period (an annual form looks at 1 January, an event-based form at its events) and refuses a period no version covers. When a form has been discontinued — a version with a Valid To and no successor — the message says so and, where the form knows it, names what replaced it. The versions are readable by every internal user and maintained by Employees / Administrator; normally you never edit them.

Company settings

The company form of a Czech or Slovak company has a Payroll Reporting tab. For a Czech company it holds the employer identification the ČSSZ forms need: the ČSSZ variable symbol (VS) and the OSSZ code of the locally competent district social security administration. The forms refuse to generate without them. Other modules add their own fields to the same tab.

Delivery and receipts

Mark Submitted records that someone filed the XML, and opens a submission for it in Draft — the record that holds how the XML reached the authority, whether it was accepted, and the receipts that prove it. It is l10n_cssk_submission_base's, which every payroll declaration uses; find it under Accounting → Reporting → Statutory Reports → Submissions. See Filing a return there.

Limitations

  • Corrections to earlier months are not separated. A payslip is counted in the month of its own period. A back payment or correction entered on this month's payslip for an earlier month is reported in this month; it does not produce, and is not moved into, an amendment of the earlier month. An amendment is generated from the amended month's payslips as they stand, not as a difference against what was filed, so a Supplementary filing contains the full figures unless the form's own template handles it. Compare the amendment with the filed copy before sending it.
  • The year can be chosen from 2020 to next year.
  • Submission is recorded, not performed. Nothing is sent to an authority by this module or the forms built on it.
  • The schema check proves the shape, not the figures. Reconcile the first filing of every form by hand.
